newsitem.title: LEBANON: Japanese guerrilla to celebrate Lod attack in Beirut jail.
newsitem.headline: Japanese guerrilla to celebrate Lod attack in Beirut jail.

text.p: A Japanese Red Army guerrilla awaiting trial in a Lebanese jail has ordered sweets and flowers for his fellow-inmates to celebrate the 25th anniversary of an anti-Israel operation in which 24 people were killed, his lawyer said on Thursday.

Bshara Abou Saad told Reuters that Kozo Okamoto, who carried out the May 1972 shootout at Tel Aviv's Lod airport, had ordered 12 kg of baklawa and flowers to distribute on Friday to prisoners in the jail of Roumieh, east of Beirut.
"They have been delivered in preparation for the celebration tomorrow. As you know prisoners meet at lunchtime so this is when the celebration will take place," Abou Saad said.

Okamoto and four other Japanese -- Kazua Tohira, Haruo Wako, Masao Adachi and Mariko Yamamoto -- were charged on April 3 in Beirut with passport forgery and other offences carrying up to 10 years in prison. They will stand trial on June 9.
Lebanon arrested the five on February 15 and decided to put them on trial in the country despite Japanese hopes of extraditing them to face international charges arising from guerrilla activity.
Okamoto was captured by Israeli forces and sentenced to life imprisonment after the Lod attack which also wounded 100 people. He was handed over in a Palestinian-Israeli prisoner swap in May, 1985.
The Red Army, founded in 1971, was allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions.
The Bekaa Valley was a haven during Lebanon's 1975-1990 civil war for guerrilla groups including Lebanese Moslems and Marxists, Palestinians, Kurds and the Red Army.
